city_center.name: Downtown Kansas City / River Market
city_center.landmark: The River Market and downtown bluffs above the Missouri River; the city's fountains and brick warehouse districts carved from the river bluffs
city_center.notes: Kansas City grew on the bluffs of the Missouri River; Irish brickworks carved out River Market and downtown streets and built the historic brick churches and warehouses. Kansas City-style barbecue -- slow-smoked meat with thick tomato-molasses sauce -- originated here in the early 20th century. sources: Kansas City brickworks / Missouri River bluffs (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Donnelly); Kansas City-style barbecue (en.wikipedia.org).

cultural_notes: Kansas City grew on the bluffs of the Missouri River; Irish immigrant brickworks carved out River Market and downtown streets from the bluffs and built the historic downtown Catholic churches -- brick is the region's foundational building material (source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Donnelly)

Kansas City-style barbecue -- slowly smoked meat, burnt ends, thick tomato-and-molasses sauce -- originated in Kansas City in the early 20th century and is a defining regional food identity (source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City-style_barbecue)

Hy-Vee is a major midwestern chain that ranks first or second across the plains states and competes with Price Chopper and Cosentino's in the Kansas City metro; Hy-Vee is employee-owned, a regional-loyalty cue (source: supermarketnews.com Kroger-Hy-Vee Midwest; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hy-Vee)

the metro straddles the Missouri-Kansas state line, and its civic identity mixes heartland-prairie, river-port, and jazz-and-barbecue culture -- creative should read cross-state, not single-state (INFERRED framing from region knowledge -- verify before production use)
